method: Per PR: a blind expert hunt from the diff and code; every candidate (the hunt, the AACR references with hand labels, and every comment any reviewer posted in our runs, anonymised) checked against the code, merged and graded, exclusions recorded; an adversarial critic per set spot-checked inclusions, exclusions and merges, and its 12 corrections were applied (2026-09-26).

vllm-project__vllm@3fe1893.pr_summary: The PR adds a new hook, `BaseProcessingInfo.get_max_tokens_per_item()` (processing.py:1103). It takes no arguments and returns None by default. `MultiModalProfiler.get_mm_max_tokens(seq_len, mm_counts)` (profiling.py:251-261) now returns the hook's result when it is not None, and skips building and processing dummy inputs. `Qwen2VLProcessingInfo` overrides the hook (qwen2_vl.py:822-823) with the constant `{"image": 16384, "video": 98304}`, which cuts about 40s from Qwen2/2.5-VL startup. The constants match only one configuration: Qwen2.5-VL with the checkpoint-default max_pixels (12845056) and max_model_len=128000, with image and video both enabled (video = 12 frames = 6 temporal groups x 16384). They ignore seq_len and mm_counts, which bound the video frame count. They also ignore the processor's configured min/max_pixels. Qwen2_5_VLProcessingInfo and Qwen2_5OmniThinkerProcessingInfo both inherit them, and the Omni class loses its "audio" entry. Every consumer reads these numbers: the V1 encoder compute/cache budget (and its disable_chunked_mm_input check, which TPU forces), the GPU/TPU runners' encoder profiling, and V0's get_max_multimodal_tokens.

defects.title: Hardcoded video bound (98304) ignores seq_len/mm_counts: wrong encoder budget for every context other than 128k (inflated 6x for Qwen2-VL's 32k, startup ValueError under disable_chunked_mm_input/TPU, under-profiled encoder memory; undersized for video-only long context)
defects.statement: The old path took the per-video maximum from a dummy video whose frame count came from `get_num_frames_with_most_features(seq_len, mm_counts)`. The new hook takes neither argument, and `get_mm_max_tokens` returns it before looking at them, so every Qwen2/2.5-VL/Omni config reports 98304 video tokens. That is correct only at max_model_len=128000 with images enabled. With a 32k context (the Qwen2-VL and Qwen2.5-Omni default, or any shorter --max-model-len) the old value was 16384. The V1 encoder compute and cache budget therefore grows about 6x beyond what profile_run measures, and startup raises a ValueError with disable_chunked_mm_input (forced on TPU) unless max_num_batched_tokens >= 98304. In a video-only 128k config the true bound (114688) is now under-reported, so such a video can never be scheduled.
defects.evidence: Head qwen2_vl.py:822-823 is `def get_max_tokens_per_item(self) -> Mapping[str, int]: return {"image": 16384, "video": 98304}`. profiling.py:256-258 is `max_tokens_per_item = self.processing_info.get_max_tokens_per_item(); if max_tokens_per_item is not None: return max_tokens_per_item`, which returns before `seq_len`/`mm_counts` are used. The removed path was `self._get_dummy_mm_inputs(seq_len, mm_counts)`, with frames from qwen2_vl.py:938-952: `max_total_frames = self._get_max_video_frames(seq_len - max_image_tokens)`, `min(max_total_frames // max(max_videos, 1), _MAX_FRAMES_PER_VIDEO)` with _MAX_FRAMES_PER_VIDEO=16. registry.py:129-137 passes `seq_len = model_config.max_model_len` and mm_counts {modality: 1 for enabled}. At the default max_pixels each temporal group of 2 frames costs 16384 tokens. So seq_len=128000 gives 12 frames = 98304 (the constant). seq_len=32768 gives 2 frames = 16384. Video-only at 128000 gives 14 frames = 114688. encoder_cache_manager.py:137-148: `if (scheduler_config.disable_chunked_mm_input and max_tokens_per_mm_item > scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens): raise ValueError(...)`, then `encoder_compute_budget = max(scheduler_config.max_num_encoder_input_tokens, max_tokens_per_mm_item)` and likewise encoder_cache_size. tpu.py:159-164 forces `scheduler_config.disable_chunked_mm_input = True` for multimodal models. gpu_model_runner.py profile_run takes `max(...)` (video, 98304), computes `cdiv(encoder_budget, max_tokens_per_mm_item)` = 1 item, and builds the dummy with `get_decoder_dummy_data(seq_len=self.max_num_tokens, mm_counts={video: 1})`, a 1-frame video of about 16384 tokens. It therefore profiles 16384 encoder tokens while the scheduler (scheduler.py:188 `encoder_budget = self.max_num_encoder_input_tokens`) admits 98304 per step. scheduler.py:678-693 sets num_new_tokens=0 for an item larger than the budget or cache, and no front-end check exists, so an oversized item stalls. Path: V1 startup `Scheduler.__init__` / `GPUModelRunner.__init__` → `compute_encoder_budget` → `get_max_tokens_per_item_by_nonzero_modality` → `get_mm_max_tokens`.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the fixed video bound (98304), or the fast path that discards seq_len/mm_counts, no longer depends on the context length or the number of items, while the old dummy path bounded video frames by seq_len. It must also name a consequence: an inflated or wrong encoder budget or cache for shorter contexts (e.g. Qwen2-VL's 32k), a startup ValueError with disable_chunked_mm_input or on TPU when max_num_batched_tokens < 98304, encoder memory the profiler never measured or OOM, or an under-reported bound so a video can never be scheduled. A generic 'hardcoded values ignore the model config, derive them' comment counts only if it names the sequence-length / frame-count / max_model_len dependency. Near-misses that do NOT count: asking to turn the literals into named constants (ref 0); a docstring 'per item' wording note (ref 2); ref 3's first bullet, which claims the result should be summed and multiplied by counts. That bullet is wrong because the caller wants per-item values; ref 3 matches this defect only through its second bullet. A bare 'please add a test' also does not count.

defects.title: Hardcoded image bound (16384) ignores the configured min/max_pixels (mm_processor_kwargs / preprocessor config): budget inflated for memory-saving configs, too small for raised max_pixels, so large images stall
defects.statement: The old image maximum came from a dummy image resized with `image_processor.max_pixels`, which honours `--mm-processor-kwargs` and the checkpoint's preprocessor config. The constant 16384 (and the 98304 video bound built on it) is right only for the default 12845056 pixels. A common memory-saving setting, e.g. max_pixels=1280*28*28, makes each image about 1280 tokens. The encoder budget is still sized to 98304, while profile_run measures one small dummy item, so far more encoder work per step is admitted than was profiled (OOM risk). Raising max_pixels with video disabled has the opposite effect: an image larger than max(max_num_batched_tokens, 16384) tokens can never be allocated in the encoder cache, and the request stalls forever.
defects.evidence: qwen2_vl.py:779-780: `if mm_config.mm_processor_kwargs: kwargs.update(mm_config.mm_processor_kwargs)` feeds `get_image_processor()` (:803). `_get_vision_info` calls `smart_resize(..., min_pixels=image_processor.min_pixels, max_pixels=image_processor.max_pixels)` (:845-850), and `get_max_image_tokens()` (:908) relied on it. The override at :822-823 returns the constant 16384 regardless. encoder_cache_manager.py:145-148: `encoder_compute_budget = max(scheduler_config.max_num_encoder_input_tokens, max_tokens_per_mm_item)` and `encoder_cache_size = max(scheduler_config.encoder_cache_size, max_tokens_per_mm_item)`, with config.py:2193-2194 defaulting both to max_num_batched_tokens. In scheduler.py:678-693, `if (not self.encoder_cache_manager.can_allocate(request, i) or num_encoder_tokens > encoder_budget)` and `num_computed_tokens >= start_pos` leads to `num_new_tokens = 0`, and the running loop at :223-227 just `continue`s every step. The front end (v1/engine/processor.py) has no check of item size against the encoder cache. For small max_pixels, gpu_model_runner.profile_run builds its one dummy item through the real, configured processor, so what it profiles is far smaller than the 98304-token budget.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the fixed image bound (or both constants) does not follow the configured image processor size (max_pixels/min_pixels/size from mm_processor_kwargs or preprocessor_config), and name a consequence: an image larger than the reported bound exceeds the encoder budget or cache and cannot be scheduled or stalls, or a smaller max_pixels gives a budget that no longer matches what is profiled. A comment that names both the max_pixels and the seq_len dependency (e.g. R2) counts for both D1 and D2. Near-misses that do NOT count: 'use named constants'; 'verify the numbers' with no mention of processor/pixel configuration; requests for tests.

defects.title: Qwen2.5-Omni thinker inherits the Qwen2-VL constant and loses its "audio" modality; an audio-only config gets a zero encoder budget and audio requests never finish
defects.statement: `Qwen2_5OmniThinkerProcessingInfo(Qwen2AudioProcessingInfo, Qwen2_5_VLProcessingInfo)` supports audio, image and video, but its MRO resolves the new hook to `Qwen2VLProcessingInfo.get_max_tokens_per_item`. The returned map therefore has no "audio" key, where the old dummy-processing path reported one. With image and video disabled (`limit_mm_per_prompt={audio: N, image: 0, video: 0}`), the non-zero filter yields an empty dict. The encoder budget and cache become (0, 0), profiling is skipped, and every audio item fails the `num_encoder_tokens > encoder_budget` check, so the request stalls forever. Audio is also dropped from V0's get_max_multimodal_tokens sum.
defects.evidence: qwen2_5_omni_thinker.py:129-130 is `class Qwen2_5OmniThinkerProcessingInfo(Qwen2AudioProcessingInfo, Qwen2_5_VLProcessingInfo):` and :175-176 is `get_supported_mm_limits` returning `{"audio": None, "image": None, "video": None}`. None of Omni, Qwen2AudioProcessingInfo or Qwen2_5_VLProcessingInfo (qwen2_5_vl.py:778) defines `get_max_tokens_per_item`, and the C3 MRO puts Qwen2VLProcessingInfo before BaseProcessingInfo. The result is `{"image": 16384, "video": 98304}`. registry.py:153-160 filters `if mm_limits[key] > 0`, so an audio-only limit yields {}. encoder_cache_manager.py:127-132: `if not max_tokens_by_modality_dict: logger.warning("All non-text modalities ... explicitly disabled ... Encoder cache will not be initialized."); return 0, 0`. scheduler.py:678-693 then sees `num_encoder_tokens > encoder_budget` (0) on every step and sets num_new_tokens to stop before the audio placeholder, or to 0 once it is reached. The old path ran the Omni dummy builder with mm_counts {audio: 1}, which does produce audio placeholders.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that Qwen2.5-Omni (the thinker's processing info) inherits the Qwen2-VL override, so the returned map lacks "audio". It must also name the consequence: audio is missing from the encoder budget, and with only audio enabled the budget is empty or zero and audio requests cannot be scheduled. Dataset ref 1's hand label mentions the missing audio key, but its note does not; a reviewer matching only ref 1's note text does NOT find this. Near-misses that do NOT count: a comment that only says subclasses (Qwen2.5-VL) inherit the constants, with no mention of audio or Omni.

excluded.reason: Style nit: asks to replace the literals 16384/98304 with named constants. Naming them fixes nothing; the substantive problem (hard-coding at all) is D1/D2.

Docstring wording nit ('for each modality' vs 'per item') at processing.py:1103-1104. The method name already says per_item and the only caller passes mm_counts=1 per modality; no behavioural consequence.
Requests to add regression tests for the profiling shortcut. Test requests are not defects; the underlying bound errors are captured as D1/D2/D3.

Clarifying question about the dummy processing that remains in profile_run. That remaining call is intentional: it builds the actual profiling batch sized by max_num_tokens, a different and smaller dummy than the two get_mm_max_tokens passes the PR removes. The PR does skip both max-token passes it describes, so no defect follows.

n8n-io__n8n@9321691.pr_summary: Adds an optional N8N_RELEASE_DATE env var (GenericConfig.releaseDate, parsed by a new Date branch in the @Env decorator) and passes it from BaseCommand.init into ErrorReporter.init. The reporter skips Sentry init when the release is more than 6 weeks old. Otherwise it schedules a setTimeout that sets enabled=false when the release reaches 6 weeks, and beforeSend drops events once that happens. The release workflow and the n8n Dockerfile are meant to bake the release date into the published image as a build arg, an ENV and an OCI `created` label.

defects.title: setTimeout overflow disables Sentry reporting about 1 ms after startup for releases younger than about 17 days
defects.statement: releaseExpiresInMs can be as large as SIX_WEEKS_IN_MS (3,628,800,000 ms), which is more than Node's maximum timer delay of 2^31-1 ms (about 24.8 days). Node clamps an overflowing delay to 1 ms and emits a TimeoutOverflowWarning. For any release less than about 17 days old, the callback therefore runs almost immediately. It sets enabled=false and logs the expiry warning, and beforeSend then drops every event. Fresh releases stop reporting right away, which is the opposite of what the PR intends.
defects.evidence: error-reporter.ts:26 `const SIX_WEEKS_IN_MS = 6 * 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;` gives 3,628,800,000. :83 `const releaseExpiresInMs = releaseDate.getTime() + SIX_WEEKS_IN_MS - Date.now();`. :89-92 `setTimeout(() => { this.enabled = false; this.logger.warn(RELEASE_EXPIRATION_WARNING); }, releaseExpiresInMs);`. :142 `if (!this.enabled) return null;`. Verified in Node with a release date 5 days old: the delay was 3196799999, Node printed 'TimeoutOverflowWarning ... Timeout duration was set to 1', and the callback fired after 2 ms. Reached from BaseCommand.init (base-command.ts:66-75), which runs for every start, worker and webhook process whenever a valid N8N_RELEASE_DATE is set, i.e. the intended production path once the release date is supplied correctly.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the setTimeout delay (up to 6 weeks) exceeds Node's 32-bit/2^31-1 ms (~24.8 day) timer limit, so the timer fires immediately or almost immediately and disables reporting for fresh releases. A generic 'use a timestamp check in beforeSend instead of setTimeout' with no mention of the overflow does not count. Neither does a comment that only notes the timer is not cleared or unref'd.

defects.title: Release workflow passes the literal `$(date ...)` string as N8N_RELEASE_DATE, so published images never get a usable release date
defects.statement: docker/build-push-action's `build-args` input is not evaluated by a shell, so no command substitution happens. N8N_RELEASE_DATE is set to the literal text `$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")`, and the Dockerfile bakes that text into ENV N8N_RELEASE_DATE and the org.opencontainers.image.created label. At runtime Date.parse returns NaN, so the decorator logs 'Invalid timestamp value for N8N_RELEASE_DATE: $(date ...)' on every process start and releaseDate stays undefined. The expiry logic never runs in published images, so the PR's stated goal is not met, and every image carries a bogus `created` label.
defects.evidence: release-publish.yml:98-106 `uses: docker/build-push-action@v6.11.0` / `with:` / `build-args: |` / `N8N_RELEASE_DATE=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")`. Action inputs only get `${{ }}` expression evaluation, and the action passes each build-arg to buildx argv with no shell. Dockerfile:13 `LABEL org.opencontainers.image.created=${N8N_RELEASE_DATE}` and :18 `ENV N8N_RELEASE_DATE=${N8N_RELEASE_DATE}`. decorators.ts:59-61 `const timestamp = Date.parse(value); if (isNaN(timestamp)) { console.warn(...)`. Verified in Node: Date.parse('$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")') is NaN. error-reporter.ts:82 `if (releaseDate)` is therefore never entered.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that `$(date ...)` in the build-push-action `build-args` input is not shell-evaluated, so the literal string, not a timestamp, reaches the image. Saying the feature is then inert (or that the value is invalid) is enough. Near-misses that do not count: generic remarks that the date may be missing or empty with no mention of the literal substitution (that is D4), and remarks that the release date should come from the npm publish step without identifying that the current value is literal.

defects.title: Expiry check runs before the `!dsn` return, so instances without Sentry configured log 'Error tracking disabled' warnings
defects.statement: The releaseDate block (early return with a warning, or a timer that warns) sits before `if (!dsn) return;`. Any process with a release date but no Sentry DSN still runs it: backendDsn defaults to '', which covers ordinary self-hosted installs. On a release older than 6 weeks, such a process logs 'Error tracking disabled because this release is older than 6 weeks.' on every start. Otherwise the timer logs it when it fires, which D1 makes immediate for fresh releases. Error tracking was never enabled on these processes, so the warning is misleading, and they also create a pointless timer.
defects.evidence: error-reporter.ts:82-93 `if (releaseDate) { ... if (releaseExpiresInMs <= 0) { this.logger.warn(RELEASE_EXPIRATION_WARNING); return; } setTimeout(() => { this.enabled = false; this.logger.warn(RELEASE_EXPIRATION_WARNING); }, releaseExpiresInMs); }` is followed at :95 by `if (!dsn) return;`. sentry.config.ts:6-7 `@Env('N8N_SENTRY_DSN') backendDsn: string = '';`. BaseCommand.init (base-command.ts:66-75) always passes releaseDate, whether or not a DSN is set. This is reachable wherever N8N_RELEASE_DATE is valid, which after D2 is fixed means every official Docker install.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the release-expiry logic runs before or regardless of the DSN check, so processes without a Sentry DSN still get the expiry warning and/or timer, and that it should sit after `if (!dsn) return`. R15's nit (move the empty-DSN return ahead of expiry scheduling) counts even though its stated keep-alive consequence is weak, since CLI commands exit via finally(). A comment that only asks for tests does not count.

defects.title: Dockerfile always sets N8N_RELEASE_DATE, so images built without the arg get an empty value and warn at every start
defects.statement: `ARG N8N_RELEASE_DATE` has no default, but `ENV N8N_RELEASE_DATE=${N8N_RELEASE_DATE}` runs unconditionally. An image built without that build arg therefore has N8N_RELEASE_DATE set to an empty string, and an empty `created` label. The README's documented build command (`--build-arg N8N_VERSION=<VERSION>` only) produces exactly this. readEnv returns '' because the variable is present in process.env, Date.parse('') is NaN, and every process start prints 'Invalid timestamp value for N8N_RELEASE_DATE: '.
defects.evidence: Dockerfile:7 `ARG N8N_RELEASE_DATE` has no default, unlike N8N_VERSION, which is validated at :5. :13 `LABEL org.opencontainers.image.created=${N8N_RELEASE_DATE}` and :18 `ENV N8N_RELEASE_DATE=${N8N_RELEASE_DATE}`. decorators.ts:18 `if (envName in process.env) return process.env[envName];` then :59-61 Date.parse and console.warn on NaN. docker/images/n8n/README.md:194 documents `docker buildx build ... --build-arg N8N_VERSION=<VERSION>` with no release date. Verified in Node: Date.parse('') is NaN.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that when the N8N_RELEASE_DATE build arg is not provided, the Dockerfile still sets an empty ENV (and label), which produces an invalid or empty value, a warning, or a missing default. Suggesting a default, validation, or guarding the ENV all count if the empty-value consequence is identified. The literal `$(date ...)` problem is D2, not this. Generic 'add validation' remarks that name no consequence are borderline and should be judged on whether they identify the empty value.

defects.title: Task-runner error reporting never gets the release date, so runners keep reporting to Sentry for expired releases
defects.statement: The expiry logic lives in the shared ErrorReporter, but TaskRunnerSentry.initIfEnabled calls errorReporter.init without releaseDate. The runner's SentryConfig does not read N8N_RELEASE_DATE, and neither the internal runner's env passthrough nor the Docker launcher's allowed-env list forwards it, while N8N_SENTRY_DSN is forwarded. On a release older than 6 weeks with a DSN configured, the main process stops reporting but task-runner processes keep sending errors to Sentry. The six-week cutoff therefore covers only part of the backend.
defects.evidence: task-runner-sentry.ts:22-29 `await this.errorReporter.init({ serverType: 'task_runner', dsn, release: n8nVersion, environment, serverName: deploymentName, beforeSendFilter: this.filterOutUserCodeErrors });` passes no releaseDate. task-runner-process.ts:55-66 passthroughEnvVars include 'N8N_SENTRY_DSN' but not N8N_RELEASE_DATE. n8n-task-runners.json allowed-env lists 'N8N_SENTRY_DSN' (line 26) but not N8N_RELEASE_DATE. @n8n/task-runner/src/config/sentry-config.ts has no release-date field.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the task runner's ErrorReporter/TaskRunnerSentry init does not receive the release date (or that N8N_RELEASE_DATE is not forwarded to runners), so runner errors keep reaching Sentry after six weeks. Comments about browser/frontend Sentry or about npm installs are different claims and do not count.

excluded.reason: Undefined releaseDate is the intended 'feature off' state and is already handled by `if (releaseDate)` at error-reporter.ts:82. Nothing to fix.
A documentation or naming suggestion. The config is parsed only in Node, and the intended ISO-8601 input is well-defined for Date.parse. This is a nit, not a defect.

The Date branch handles failure exactly like the Number and Boolean branches just above it (warn and keep the class default), so there is no inconsistency. The cross-platform parsing concern does not apply to Node-only config.
Speculative. The code is Node-only and the input is ISO-8601, so browser Date.parse inconsistency is irrelevant. Adding moment or luxon is a taste suggestion.
Wrong. releaseDate is never passed to Sentry. It is used only for expiry arithmetic in ErrorReporter.init.
Wrong. GlobalConfig.generic is a non-optional @Nested section that the Config factory always instantiates (decorators.ts:36-38), so it cannot be undefined.
Style. SIX_WEEKS_IN_MS is already a named, self-describing constant.

The uncaughtException listener predates this PR (diff context). When the release has expired at startup, report stays defaultReport, which logs errors, so the claimed silent swallowing is not introduced here.
Unreachable. The decorator only assigns a Date when !isNaN(timestamp), so an Invalid Date can never reach error-reporter.ts:83.
Wrong. In the already-expired case, init returns before Sentry init() and before beforeSend is registered, so leaving enabled=true has no effect and nothing is sent.

The npm installs point is a scope and design choice, not a defect. The mechanism is explicitly opt-in via env and wired only into the Docker release. npm installs report to Sentry only if the operator sets N8N_SENTRY_DSN themselves. No broken behaviour is introduced for them, since they report exactly as before.
The browser/frontend Sentry client is untouched and out of the PR's stated scope (the backend error-reporter). This is a scope question, not a defect the PR introduces.
A request to add tests. Excluded by the benchmark rules. The underlying timer bug is D1.

The request for reporter tests is excluded as a test request. Its nit about moving the empty-DSN return is credited to D3. Its claim that a pending timer keeps processes alive is not supported: BaseCommand.finally() calls this.exit, which leads oclif to call process.exit.

google-gemini__gemini-cli@c6e6248.pr_summary:
Test-only PR (#9177, "Add integration test for extensions"). It adds `TestRig.runCommand(args, {stdin})` to integration-tests/test-helper.ts, which spawns the bundled CLI with arbitrary subcommand args and optional stdin. It also adds integration-tests/extensions-install.test.ts, which writes a gemini-extension.json into the rig's test dir and pre-uninstalls `test-extension`, swallowing any error. It then runs `extensions install --path=<testDir>` (answering the consent prompt with 'y') and `extensions list`, bumps the version to 0.0.2, runs `extensions update test-extension`, and finally uninstalls the extension and calls rig.cleanup() and rmSync(testDir).

The functional flow is correct at head:
- Extension subcommands exit inside parseArguments (config.ts:343-349), before any sandbox relaunch or stdin read.
- The local-type update check compares the source version (github.ts:124-141).
- The success line of the update contains '0.0.2'.

The defects are in isolation and cleanup, plus one piece of duplication:
- The test installs into and uninstalls from the runner's real ~/.gemini/extensions. Its pre-uninstall deletes any real extension of that name.
- The final uninstall is not in a finally block.
- An unconditional rmSync overrides the documented KEEP_OUTPUT retention.
- `runCommand` is a near-verbatim copy of `run()`'s subprocess machinery.

defects.title: Test mutates the runner's real ~/.gemini/extensions, and its pre-uninstall deletes a pre-existing user `test-extension`
defects.statement: `runCommand` spawns the CLI with the parent's environment and HOME, and extension install, uninstall and update always act on `os.homedir()/.gemini/extensions`. The new test's unconditional pre-uninstall (line 28) therefore recursively deletes any real extension named `test-extension`, together with its enablement entry, on a developer's machine. The test's install, update and uninstall steps also rewrite the developer's real Gemini config. Other integration test files run in parallel, and every CLI they spawn loads that same directory while this test is changing it.
defects.evidence:
The spawn and the pre-uninstall:
- test-helper.ts:315-318 `spawn('node', commandArgs, { cwd: this.testDir!, stdio: 'pipe' })` passes no env or HOME override. `TestRig.setup` (test-helper.ts:131-161) isolates only the cwd.
- extension.ts:83-85 `static getUserExtensionsDir() { const storage = new Storage(os.homedir()); return storage.getExtensionsDir(); }`.
- uninstallExtension (extension.ts:586-606) finds the extension by name in `loadUserExtensions()` (which reads os.homedir()), calls `manager.remove(extensionName)`, then `fs.promises.rm(storage.getExtensionDir(), { recursive: true, force: true })`.
- The test at lines 27-31 runs `rig.runCommand(['extensions','uninstall','test-extension'])` unconditionally inside try/catch {}. Install (extension.ts:392-468, 485 `enableExtension(..., SettingScope.User)`) writes into the same real directory.

The harness contract and parallelism:
- The harness already treats HOME as state it must restore: globalSetup.ts:34-43 and :90-99 back up and restore ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md. Nothing does the same for extensions.
- vitest.config.ts:16 `fileParallelism: true`. Every other test's CLI runs main() -> loadExtensions() -> loadExtensionsFromDir(os.homedir()) (gemini.tsx:251, extension.ts:175-203), so it reads this directory while it is being mutated. loadExtension's `fs.statSync(extensionDir)` (extension.ts:208) sits outside the try block and can throw ENOENT in that window.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the test or `runCommand` operates on the real user home or global extension store (~/.gemini/extensions, os.homedir()) instead of an isolated one. It must also give a consequence: it deletes or overwrites a pre-existing user `test-extension` (via the pre-uninstall), pollutes the developer's real Gemini config, or interferes with parallel tests. A comment that only says 'cleanup is skipped if an assertion fails' belongs to D2, not here. A comment that only says 'the testDir cwd is not validated' does not count.

defects.title: Final uninstall is not in a finally block, so a failed step leaves test-extension installed in the real HOME
defects.statement: The only teardown uninstall (line 49), `rig.cleanup()` and rmSync run only if every earlier command and assertion succeeds. If the install, list or update assertion fails or a command rejects, `test-extension` stays installed and enabled in the runner's real ~/.gemini/extensions. The user's normal Gemini sessions and later test runs then load it. The pre-uninstall only rescues the next attempt of this same test, and a failed final retry leaves the state behind.
defects.evidence:
The throw points and the skipped teardown:

On the server, the IfBlock visitor now emits a single if / else-if / else statement with one opening marker per chain: `<!--[-->` for the first branch, `<!--[N-->` for the N-th else-if and `<!--[!-->` for the else. On the client, the IfBlock visitor passes a `$$elseif` tuple into else-if alternates and anchors the nested `$.if` on the parent's `$$anchor` instead of a `$.comment()` fragment. A new Fragment special case (a single elseif IfBlock needs no template) makes that possible, and the `{}` scope wrapper is removed. At runtime, `if_block(node, fn, [root_index, hydrate_index])` changes: the root level parses the marker (`[`, `[!` or `[N`) into an index, nested levels compare that index with their depth, and a mismatch sets the index to -1. The new `[N` marker is never added to the runtime's other hydration-marker depth walkers: `remove_nodes()`, used for mismatch recovery, and the dev `assign_locations()`. Both therefore become unbalanced whenever an else-if branch after the first was server-rendered.

microsoft__typescript-go@892b4a3.pr_summary: The PR adds a way to keep hand-edited fourslash tests out of the converter. A new script, internal/fourslash/_scripts/makeManual.mts (`npm run makemanual`), moves a generated test from tests/gen/ to tests/manual/ and adds its name to _scripts/manualTests.txt. convertFourslash.mts reads that list, skips regenerating the listed tests and creates tests/manual. It has four real defects. (1) The PR does not ship manualTests.txt, but the converter reads it unconditionally, so convertfourslash, updatefailing and the CI generate job all crash, after the gen suite has already been deleted. (2) makeManual records a filename, and the converter looks up a capitalized base name, so no listed test is ever skipped. (3) A test moved into the separate tests/manual Go package loses the util_test.go helpers it uses and fails to compile. (4) `*.txt` is gitignored with an exception only for failingTests.txt, so a manualTests.txt that makeManual creates is never committed. There is also a low-severity leftover: the converter creates the tests/manual directory for no purpose.

defects.title: convertFourslash crashes with ENOENT because manualTests.txt is never shipped and is read without an existence check
defects.statement: getManualTests() calls fs.readFileSync(manualTestsPath) without checking that the file exists, and the PR does not add internal/fourslash/_scripts/manualTests.txt. Only makeManual ever creates the file. So `npm run convertfourslash` and `npm run updatefailing` throw ENOENT on every checkout. By that point main() has already rm'd tests/gen, leaving only util_test.go, and updateFailing has already emptied failingTests.txt. The CI `generate` job, which runs `npm run updatefailing`, fails on this PR.

defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the converter's read of manualTests.txt throws (or crashes, or fails) when the file is absent, AND that the file is absent by default: the PR does not add it, or only makemanual creates it. Mentioning that updatefailing, CI or the regeneration workflow breaks is supportive but not required. Near-misses that should not count: generic advice to add try/catch or error handling around file reads with no claim that the file is missing, and comments about the .gitignore of *.txt alone, which is D4.

defects.title: makeManual records the filename, but the converter checks the capitalized test name, so manual tests are never skipped
defects.statement: makeManual joins its argument to gen/ without appending `_test.go`. To pass the existence check, the argument must be the full generated filename, e.g. `basicClassMembers_test.go`, and makeManual records that raw string in manualTests.txt. convertFourslash looks up `test.name[0].toUpperCase() + test.name.substring(1)`, e.g. `BasicClassMembers`. No argument satisfies both scripts, so the skip never fires. Every moved test is regenerated into tests/gen on the next convert or updatefailing run, and the test then exists in both gen/ and manual/. The PR's stated guarantee, 'tests in manualTests.txt will be skipped and not regenerated', does not hold. In CI, the generate job's `git diff --staged --exit-code` fails because the removed gen file comes back.
defects.evidence: makeManual.mts:16-18 `const testName = args[0]; const testFileName = testName; const genTestFile = path.join(genDir, `${testFileName}`);` has no suffix, while gen files are written as `${test.name}_test.go` (convertFourslash.mts:77). makeManual.mts:39 `manualTests.push(testName);` stores the raw argument. convertFourslash.mts:70-72 `const testName = test.name[0].toUpperCase() + test.name.substring(1); if (manualTests.has(testName)) { return; }`. For example, gen/basicClassMembers_test.go gets list entry `basicClassMembers_test.go`, but the lookup key is `BasicClassMembers`.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the identifier written to manualTests.txt, the raw argument or filename, differs from the key convertFourslash checks, the capitalized base test name, so listed tests are still regenerated or the skip does not work. A comment framed as 'the manual list is not stripped of a Test prefix the way failing tests are, so filtering may fail' is a weaker version of the same mismatch and counts only if it claims the skip or filter fails. Near-misses that should not count: saying only that makeManual should validate the argument ends in _test.go without linking it to the converter lookup; the PR-body command-name mismatch (manualtest vs makemanual); and path-traversal comments.

defects.title: Tests moved to tests/manual lose the util_test.go helpers and fail to compile
defects.statement: Generated tests use package-local helpers defined in util_test.go, such as defaultCommitCharacters, ignored, ptrTo and the completionGlobals vars. The converter copies that file only into tests/gen. makeManual moves just the one _test.go file into tests/manual, which is a separate Go package directory with no copy of the helpers. Moving any helper-using test, which covers roughly 730 of the 1308 files in gen/ (e.g. basicClassMembers_test.go), gives `undefined: defaultCommitCharacters` and similar errors. That breaks `hereby test` (`go test ./...`) and CI.

Near-misses that should not count: saying that updateFailing does not run the manual tests, which the PR body acknowledges and is not a compile failure; and generic comments that 'manual tests might break' with no helper or package mechanism.

defects.title: manualTests.txt matches the repo's `*.txt` gitignore rule, so the manual-test list is never committed
defects.statement: .gitignore ignores `*.txt` and re-includes only specific files, among them `internal/fourslash/_scripts/failingTests.txt`. defects.statement: The converter adds manualOutputDir and runs mkdirSync on it every time, but it never writes to, reads from, formats or tests that directory. elastic__elasticsearch@dc8943f.pr_summary:
The PR changes the size of the hierarchical-centroid lookahead buffer in DefaultIVFVectorsReader.getCentroidIteratorWithParents. The old buffer was a fixed 20% of all centroids (CENTROID_SAMPLING_PERCENTAGE = 0.2). The new one is bufferSize = min(max(visitRatio * numCentroids * CENTROID_OVERSAMPLING(8), 1), numCentroids). To support this, visitRatio is threaded from IVFVectorsReader.search, through the abstract getCentroidIterator, into getCentroidIteratorWithParents.

Checks at head:
- There is one implementation of the abstract method (DefaultIVFVectorsReader) and one caller (IVFVectorsReader.search:251).
- Nothing else references the removed constant, so the build is intact.
- visitRatio is validated to [0,1] when explicit, is positive and finite when dynamic, and is clamped at the use site. The parent path only runs when centroids > centroidsPerParentCluster^2, so the size cannot be 0, NaN or overflowed.

The surviving concerns are about recall and tuning, not crashes:
- The buffer now scales with visitRatio, so on the default dynamic path with small k it drops below one parent's 16-child group. Candidates from other parents are then never ranked against the top parent's children.
- The oversampling factor 8 silently hard-codes DEFAULT_CENTROIDS_PER_PARENT_CLUSTER/2.

defects.title: visitRatio-scaled centroid buffer can shrink below one parent's children group, so the hierarchical iterator stops comparing children across parents (recall risk)
defects.statement: bufferSize is now visitRatio*numCentroids*8. With the default dynamic visit ratio and small k it is only a few entries, fewer than one parent's ~16 children. The initial fill therefore expands only the top-scoring parent, and updateQueue() keeps refilling from that parent's remaining children before any other parent is opened. The search can spend its whole vector-visit budget on the top parent's children and never score a better child under another parent. Filtered and nested searches keep pulling centroids past the visitRatio budget, and those extra centroids are also taken in this coarse parent-greedy order. The old 20% buffer ranked children across dozens of parents first, so approximate-kNN recall can regress.
defects.evidence:
DefaultIVFVectorsReader.java:197 `final int bufferSize = (int) Math.min(Math.max(visitRatio * numCentroids * CENTROID_OVERSAMPLING, 1), numCentroids);` (was `Math.max(numCentroids * CENTROID_SAMPLING_PERCENTAGE, 1)`).

The initial fill at :216 is `while (parentsQueue.size() > 0 && neighborQueue.size() < bufferSize)`, with an inner loop at :231 that takes children of the current parent until the buffer is full. updateQueue() at :255-260 adds from currentParentQueue first, and only at :260-276 pops a new parent once that group is empty.

The visitRatio comes from AbstractIVFKnnVectorQuery.java:141-144 as `log10(totalVectors)^2 * max(numCands, 5k) / totalVectors`. It is computed over the whole index and applied per segment.
- Example with ten 1M-vector segments (10M total) and k=10: visitRatio ≈ 2450/1e7 = 2.45e-4. Each segment has ~2604 centroids and 16 children per parent, so the buffer is 2.45e-4*2604*8 ≈ 5, below one parent group.

The filtered loop at IVFVectorsReader.java:282 (`actualDocs < expectedScored || actualDocs < knnCollector.k()`) and the `minCompetitiveSimilarity() == NEGATIVE_INFINITY` clause at :267 both keep iterating regardless of visitRatio.

The PR body reports no recall loss in local runs, so the impact is a plausible structural degradation, not a demonstrated one.

A finding counts if it says the new visitRatio-proportional buffer can be too small, whether smaller than a parent's children group or smaller than the centroids actually visited in filtered/nested searches. It must connect that to lost cross-parent ranking (the queue refills from one parent's children, better children under other parents are never considered, the order degrades to greedy-by-parent) and so to a possible recall or quality loss compared with the old 20% buffer. Low-visit-ratio examples (R1/R2/R4) and the filtered/nested variant (hunt) both count.

IsSupportedDevice ignores `version`, and InitDevice calls HIDAPI_JoystickConnected even when feature report 0x06 fails, which is what happens on the pre-v2.05/v3.06 firmware the PR body calls unsupported. Those controllers are therefore taken away from the DInput/evdev/IOKit path and its gamepad-DB mappings, where they worked. Each packet then goes through the new fixed-offset parser: the report-ID filter drops most of them, and any whose first byte happens to be 0x01, 0x03 or 0x04 is decoded as garbage. The result is lost or garbled input for users who have not updated their firmware.

The driver's default is `true` (line 457), and SDL_HIDAPI_DEFAULT is true on desktop. HIDAPI_IsDevicePresent (SDL_hidapijoystick.c:1247) makes the other backends skip a device that a HIDAPI driver has claimed.
